info.title: AVC configuration API
info.summary: LINKIN's API for configuring, pricing and quoting aluminium profiles.
info.description:
## What this API is for

This is LINKIN's API for configuring, pricing and quoting aluminium profiles. A customer chooses a profile and its options, such as the length, the alloy and the finish. The API answers what can be chosen and what it costs, and the customer issues the priced order as a quotation or an inquiry. This reference keeps SAP's names; *SAP's words* below explains each.

## Access

Every call is signed in by LINKIN for the customers its caller may act for. A call sees only what is that customer's own: the materials and prices of its sales areas, its own profiles and its own documents. Access and credentials come through the customer's sales representative at LINKIN.

## Customers and their profiles

A **linked customer** is a company LINKIN already sells to. It has a customer number in SAP, its **sold-to party**, and its sign-in names it.

A **new customer** has registered on the LINKIN website but has no customer number yet. Its sign-in names LINKIN's **one-time customer** instead: SAP's one shared record for buyers who have none of their own. A new customer may only send inquiries, at most 20 a day. The company and contact details come from the website registration. LINKIN has not verified them.

LINKIN sells three kinds of profile:

- A customer's **own profile** has a shape, its **geometry**, made for that customer. It is pressed through a die, the steel tool that gives a profile its shape, and released to that customer only.
- A **catalogue profile** is a standard shape any customer of PROFILINK's sales area may order. PROFILINK is LINKIN's catalogue brand.
- A **new profile** is one the customer has drawn, with no die yet. It is priced as an inquiry.

A customer buys in one or more **sales areas**: the LINKIN company and the sales channel that sell to it. Own profiles are sold in `1102/10`, LINKIN's own. Catalogue profiles are sold in `1002/10`, PROFILINK's. A customer sees the materials and prices of its own sales areas only, since not every material is offered to every customer. An inquiry is the one exception: every inquiry is made in `1102/10`, wherever its customer buys.

## SAP's words

- **Material**: a product LINKIN sells, configured from options. One material may cover many profile shapes, each chosen by a field.
- **Master data**: what changes only with a new model, such as the materials, their fields and the price list.
- **Characteristic** (SAP's transaction CT04): one option of a material, such as its length or its finish. The API calls it a field, and keeps SAP's name for it, such as `ZA_LENGTH_MM`.
- **Class** (class type 300): the characteristics a family of materials is configured by.
- **Sold-to party** (`KUNNR`): a customer's number in SAP.
- **Sales area**: the sales organization and distribution channel a customer buys through, such as `1102/10`. A material's sales views (`MVKE`) say where it is sold, and its sales status what may be issued for it.
- **Quotation** (VA21) and **inquiry** (VA11): SAP's two offer documents. VA25 and VA15 list them by customer, off SAP's index `VAKPA`.
- **Reason for rejection** (`VBAP-ABGRU`, set up in OVAG): why a document's items are rejected, the same reason on every item where the whole document is rejected in VA22 or VA12. A revocation here gives one, by its code, its text beside it (`TVAGT-BEZEI`). SAP keeps no note beside it; its nearest is the document's header text (text object `VBBK`).
- **Pricing procedure** (V/08): the steps that build a price, from the metal to the finish to the minimum charges per order. Its **condition types** (V/06) are its lines, and its **condition records** (VK11) the rates.
- **Value help** (F4): the values a field allows.
- **Valuation screen**: SAP's screen where a person fills in a configurable material's options.
- **Sales order simulation**: SAP pricing a sales order without saving it.
- **User exits**: rules of LINKIN's own that an order runs, such as rounding a quantity up to whole packs.
- **Stock bar**: a profile kept in stock at a set length.
- **SD**: SAP's sales and distribution, where orders and prices live.

## Technical detail

What the API says to a user interface, and only that: the materials a sales order can configure, the fields each is configured with, a customer's assortment, the price list of a customer's sales area, one document per evaluated configuration and the values of one of its fields, and several items as one sales order. SAP names survive as data — a characteristic's CT04 name, a constraint's name, an issue code.

Each call stands alone: every request carries the whole entry and every response the whole screen. A response is a pure function of the model version and the body. An issued document never changes, except for its status, and the same order issued again within a day answers the same document.

Two error channels, never mixed: an HTTP error is for the request — a body that is not JSON, a characteristic the class does not allocate, an unknown material — and everything about an entered value is inside a `200` document with a status: an entry the type refuses, or one holding a control, bidirectional or invisible character, is a `conflict` on its field, a missing one is `required`, a value a dependency rejects is a `conflict` with the rule that rejects it.

An HTTP error is an `ApiError`: its code and message, whether the same request may succeed later (`retryable`), whether repeating it is harmless (`safeToRetry`), and the id LINKIN traces the request by (`requestId`).

The static routes carry a digest of the master data as their `ETag` and answer `304` to a matching `If-None-Match`, once the call's sign-in passes the route's checks. The signed-in person's own cache alone keeps the materials, a material and the price list, never one shared between sign-ins: each is answered to a sign-in whose customers' sales areas reach it.

These routes answer what a customer reads: the lines the quotation prints, the fields an order can enter, the price list of the customer's sales area named, and the materials of the families they offer.

**The sign-in.** LINKIN signs in every call under `/customer/v1`, for the customers its caller may act for; health, under `/public/v1`, acts for none. A call acts only for those customers, an inquiry in the inquiry's own sales area whichever area the customer buys in: a sold-to party or a sales area it may not act for is `403 CUSTOMER_NOT_ALLOWED`, an unknown party alike. An issued document of another customer, read, submitted or revoked by its id, its pages among it, is the `404` of one never issued. A detail of the sign-in missing or refused is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, its message naming the detail and how to fix it. The materials and the price list are the customer's own sales areas', another area's `403 CUSTOMER_NOT_ALLOWED`; a material's fields answer a material sold in one of those areas, or the inquiry's material, any other the `404` of an unknown material.

**Representation.** Every number is a JSON number, in a request as in an answer, rounded to its scale where the API writes it and printed in its shortest digits: an amount to its currency's decimals, two in `EUR`; a quantity to its unit's, none for the piece, three for every other unit; a factor, a rate's `per` and a percentage at the precision the engine computed them. A number with a scale says `format: decimal`: read it as a decimal, never as a binary float to compute with. A count is a whole number. A request's quantity is a JSON number of at most its unit's decimals: written as a string it is refused, `INVALID_REQUEST`, and with more decimals `INVALID_QUANTITY`, each with its `pointer`. A request body names each key once in every object, its keys compared with their escapes decoded, as I-JSON requires (RFC 7493 §2.3): a body that is not JSON is `INVALID_JSON`, its message naming the line and column where it stops, and one naming a key twice in an object is `INVALID_JSON` too, its `pointer` the key's own member, as `/values/ZA_LENGTH`, its message naming the key.

A unit is its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — what UBL and cXML require — with SAP's internal key beside it, `sapUnit` (or `basisSapUnit`, `weightSapUnit` beside the unit of that name); a request names its quantity's unit, where it names one, by the Rec 20 code of the material's own. A unit whose T006 key the model cannot name yet keeps the model's spelling as its SAP key. A currency is ISO 4217's code alone: a percentage condition (calculation type `A`) carries its rate in `percentage`, without `amount` and `currency`. A day is `YYYY-MM-DD` in the sales organization's time zone, which an order's header names, `timeZone` (IANA's name, `Europe/Sofia`).

A message has one shape wherever a document carries one, `Message`: its severity, its code — SAP's message class and number where SAP issues one, the engine's documented code otherwise, each listed with its meaning — whether a buyer needs to look at the line, its text, its variables and what it is about, by key. An object's own words are its `text` — a characteristic's, a group's, a value's in a list, a message's, a line's — and the words of the value a characteristic holds its `valueText`, as SAP's external configuration carries `CHARC_TXT` and `VALUE_TXT` (`E1CUVAL`, `BAPICUVAL`). Every enumeration an answer carries is open, `x-extensible-enum`: a later minor version may add a value, and each says what a reader takes one it does not know as; a request's enumerations are closed. A boolean is always present, an optional object absent and never `null`, and a list is answered as an object holding it under its name.

tags.name: Public
tags.description: `/public/v1`: what is for anyone LINKIN signed in, acting for a customer or not. Public means open to every signed-in caller, not to the whole internet. It holds the health check only; everything else is behind the customer's sign-in.

tags.name: Service
tags.description: Whether the service is up, and on which model, for a monitor to call.

tags.name: Customer
tags.description: `/customer/v1`: everything a customer does. It shows what the customer can order and at what rates, prices a profile or a whole order, issues quotations and inquiries, and reads them back. Every call must carry the customer's sign-in, which LINKIN writes. A call without it is refused, and the refusal says why. A call acts only for the customers its sign-in names. The MCP server, `/customer/mcp`, sits beside them and runs them for a customer's AI assistant.

tags.name: Master data
tags.description: What a customer can order, and at what rates: the materials sold in its sales areas, each material's fields, the customer's own list of profiles, and the price list. Master data changes only when LINKIN publishes a new model, so a browser may keep a copy for a while. Each route answers the customer's own sales areas only, since not every material is offered to every customer.

tags.name: Configuration
tags.description: One profile configured: its fields checked and priced as a person fills them in, and the values one field allows. Nothing is saved: each call sends everything chosen so far.

tags.name: Order
tags.description: A whole order priced, then issued as a document. Pricing comes first, so the customer sees the exact price before anything is issued. A quotation is for profiles LINKIN can make today. An inquiry, a preliminary offer, is for new profiles that need a new die.

tags.name: Issuing
tags.description: A priced order issued as a quotation or an inquiry, and what its customer may do with it after: submit a quotation to LINKIN, which is final, or revoke a draft quotation or an open inquiry, giving a reason.

tags.name: Issued documents
tags.description: An issued quotation or inquiry read back: as two pages for a person, the summary and the details, or as data for a program. Each answers its own customer only. It never changes, except for its status.

tags.name: History
tags.description: A customer's quotations and inquiries, newest first, to find one again. The MCP server's tools read them.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: Also run by LINKIN's MCP server: one of its tools, or a document page it serves, calls this operation for a customer's AI assistant.

get.summary: The service is up, and on which model
get.description:
Tells a monitor that the service is up. It also names the model version: the version of LINKIN's products, rules and prices the API holds. It is for anyone LINKIN signed in, acting for a customer or not. It is the only route outside the customer's sign-in.

The model version and id, how many materials are sold.

get.summary: The customer's assortment: its own geometries, then the catalogue
get.description:
Lists the exact profiles one customer can order in one of its sales areas: its own profiles in LINKIN's area, the catalogue profiles in PROFILINK's. Each names the material and the values that order it, its packs, the lengths it is cut to and the stock bars kept. The materials list is the same for every customer of an area; this list is the customer's own. The MCP server reads it to offer a customer its profiles. A customer reads only its own, since its own profiles are released to it only.

What the sold-to party orders in the sales area, paged: its own geometries first — its rows of the plant's release list, in the list's order, each ordered as the material that takes a geometry from the list — then the catalogue profiles sold in the area, each a material whose classification gives its geometry. Each with its geometry and text, the order line it is, its packs per finish off the packaging list, its lengths and longest bar, the stock list's bars, the minimums per order it is grouped under, its weight per metre and its perimeter; beside the list the bar rules, as data. A list, not availability. The packs: each line's quantity is lifted to the smallest `minimum` of its finish's packs, side 1's on an assembly — a catalogue article made to length, at a length not among its `stockLengths`, to at least 600 — then rounded up, whole steps of the largest `rounding`, the rest one step of the smallest `rounding` at least as large; `pieces` only counts packs, the last possibly part-full. Coated `PACK` with `minimum` 1, `rounding` 1 and `pieces` 12: 244 pieces stay 244, packed as 21 x PACK; bare `AW1`, `AW1/2` and `AW1/3`, each with `minimum`, `rounding` and `pieces` of 180, 72 and 27: 200 become 207, 1 x AW1 and 1 x AW1/3. Send the pieces wanted; the order rounds them.

A page of the assortment, and the bar rules.

parameters.name: soldToParty
parameters.description: `VBAK-KUNNR`, the customer the assortment is for: at most 10 characters, digits alone read with their leading zeros. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

parameters.name: salesOrganization
parameters.description: `VBAK-VKORG`, given together with `distributionChannel`, both required.

parameters.name: distributionChannel
parameters.description: `VBAK-VTWEG`, given together with `salesOrganization`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `next` a page answered: the page after it. Opaque, versioned and holding a position alone; one for another party or sales area, or none the API wrote, is refused, `INVALID_CURSOR`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most profiles the page holds, a whole number from 1 to 200; 25 where omitted.

Cache-Control.description: `no-store`: one customer's own, answered to a sign-in its URL does not carry.

400.description: `INVALID_REQUEST`: no `soldToParty`, or one of more than 10 characters or holding a control, bidirectional or invisible character; neither sales area parameter, or one without the other; a `limit` other than a whole number from 1 to 200; a parameter the query does not take, `pointer` its name; a parameter given twice. `INVALID_CURSOR`: an `after` the API did not write for this party and sales area, `pointer` `/after`. First, `INVALID_REQUEST` with no `pointer` for a call without the sign-in, with one LINKIN did not write, or with its person's details refused; then the same for the details of the customer the call acts for, or whose document it reads, refused. `UNKNOWN_SALES_AREA`: no material is sold in the sales area.

403.description: `CUSTOMER_NOT_ALLOWED`: the call names a sold-to party or a sales area the sign-in may not act for: a customer it is not linked to and an unknown party alike, so nothing is learnt of another customer; a quotation, or another party than LINKIN's one-time customer, for a sign-in linked to none, which asks for inquiries alone; or an inquiry in another sales area than the inquiry's. `pointer` `/soldToParty`, or `/salesOrganization` where the sign-in may act for the party, or for one of its own where none is named, in another sales area alone. Checked after the sales area and before the sold-to party is looked up; nothing is evaluated, listed or issued.

500.description: `INTERNAL`: the cause is logged, never sent.

get.summary: The materials a sales order can configure, in the customer's sales area
get.description:
Lists the materials a customer can order in one of its sales areas. A material is a configurable product: one may cover many profile shapes, each chosen by a field. The MCP server reads it to know which materials can be ordered. It answers only a sales area the customer buys in, since not every material is offered to every customer: own profiles and catalogue profiles are sold in different areas. Another area is refused.

Every material a sales order can configure that the customer's routes offer in the customer's sales area the query names, with its family — the class type 300 — its unit and its sales areas, a page of them with `next` while more remain and `total` on every page. The sales area is one the sign-in acts in for one of its customers: the sold-to party's sales areas divide the materials it may order, LINKIN's from PROFILINK's. A material of a family the customer's routes do not offer is no such material here. A page of at most `limit` materials, 200 where omitted: while the answer has a `next`, call again with it as `after`, in the same sales area, until a page answers none: the pages joined are the list.

parameters.description: `VBAK-VKORG`, required with `distributionChannel`: the materials sold in that distribution chain, the customer's.

parameters.name: distributionChannel
parameters.description: `VBAK-VTWEG`, given together with `salesOrganization`.

parameters.description: The `next` a page answered: the page after it. Opaque, versioned and holding a position alone; one for another sales area, or none the API wrote, is refused, `INVALID_CURSOR`.

parameters.description: The most a page holds, a whole number from 1 to 200; 200 where omitted.

get.summary: A material: its fields, as CT04, its class and its configuration profile define them
get.description:
Describes one material: every field a customer fills in to order it, and the values each allows. The MCP server reads it to know what to ask the customer. It answers only a material sold in one of the customer's sales areas, or the inquiry material, the one material every new profile is priced as. Any other material answers as if it did not exist, so a customer learns nothing of what is sold to others.

The material as master data defines it before anything is entered, in no sales area: its family, the class type 300; its unit; its sales areas (MVKE); `readsSoldToParty`, whether the order header's sold-to party reaches its configuration; and its `fields` in screen order, the CT04 characteristics an order can enter and those a printed line bills by (`notReadyForInput`), each with its format, control, Values tab, interval, unit, group and input control. No price: an entry's screen and price are `configure_item`'s.

The material — its family, unit and sales areas — and its fields as the customer reads them, in screen order: the characteristics an order can enter and those a priced line bills by, each with its type, control, Values tab, interval, unit, group and input control. A material sold in a sales area the sign-in acts in for one of its customers, or the inquiry's material; any other is answered as no such material.

get.summary: The price list of the customer's sales area
get.description:
The price list a customer reads: every rate LINKIN charges in one of its sales areas, process by process, from the metal and the press to the finish and the minimum charges. It answers only a sales area the customer buys in. Every customer of an area has the same rates.

The sales area's pricing procedure (V/08) read as the customer's price list: one process per block, closed by its subtotal; in each, the condition types (V/06) V/08 prints and the minimums per order the printed lines are billed at the least of, `perOrder` and `statistical` marked; each condition record (VK11) a rate — its variant key or key values, amount or percentage, pricing unit, scale, and the characteristic it is multiplied by (`$SET_PRICING_FACTOR`). No routines and no access sequences. Rates, not an order's price: that is `evaluate_order`'s.

The pricing procedure the sales area runs, read as the customer's price list: the meters their documents show — those V/08 prints, and the minimums per order the printed lines are billed at the least of — each at its rates, without the routines and access sequences. The sales area is one the sign-in acts in for one of its customers: the price list is the customer's, the same for every customer of the area.

post.description:
Checks and prices one profile while a person fills in its fields, as SAP's valuation screen does. It is for a program that configures one item before ordering, such as a webshop someone builds, calling it after each change. The answer lists the fields still needed, the values that clash and why, and the price so far. Nothing is saved. A wrong value is shown on its field, to be corrected there, rather than refusing the call.

One item's configuration as VCP's valuation screen evaluates it, nothing kept: the whole entry — `values` by CT04 name, `quantity`, the sales area and, where the material's `readsSoldToParty`, the sold-to party — answered as the screen the customer reads: its `status` (`ok`, `incomplete`, `inconsistent`); each field with its status, value, what decided it and, on a list field open to input, up to 50 options with `optionCount`; the item as the user exits left it, its quantity lifted to its minimum and rounded up by its packs as `list_assortment` says, never to whole packs of `pieces`, with the pricing V/08 prints; the issues; and `lock`. A value problem is a status on its field, never an error. A longer list is `find_values`'; several items priced together, `evaluate_order`'s.

The screen as a customer reads it, whatever the entry: the lines the quotation prints; the fields an order can enter and those a printed line bills by; on a material that reads the sold-to party no value the entries rule out but the field's own. A value problem is a status on its field, never an error.

parameters.name: material
parameters.description: The material number of a material a sales order configures.

400.description: `INVALID_JSON`; `INVALID_REQUEST`, among it a field the body does not take, no `quantity`, no sales area, and no `soldToParty` where the material reads it; `INVALID_QUANTITY`; `UNKNOWN_CHARACTERISTIC` for a name the material's class does not allocate or an order cannot enter; or `MATERIAL_NOT_IN_SALES_AREA` for a distribution chain the material is not sold in, one sold in another sales area the sign-in acts in. First, `INVALID_REQUEST` with no `pointer` for a call without the sign-in, with one LINKIN did not write, or with its person's details refused; then the same for the details of the customer the call acts for, or whose document it reads, refused. `UNKNOWN_SALES_AREA`: no material is sold in the sales area. `UNKNOWN_SOLD_TO_PARTY` (`pointer` `/soldToParty`): the customer master holds no record of the sold-to party (`KNA1`; SAP's `VP 199`), or does not extend it to the sales area (`KNVV`; `VP 197`) — refused at the header, before any line. A request naming no party is priced without one.

post.summary: Plan the trucks: how much fits, to size the order
post.description:
Loads a customer's profiles onto standard trucks, as an estimate of how much fits by weight and by size, to size the order: not a loading plan. LINKIN's prices are ex works, so the customer's carrier brings the truck. It is for a customer, or the MCP server on its behalf, to see how many trucks its lines being priced and its issued quotations take, any mix. Nothing is kept or priced, and the plan is on no issued document. Every line and quotation item given is loaded, or nothing is.

The body is the customer — `soldToParty` required, with its sales area — the lines to plan, as `POST /customer/v1/order` takes them, up to 300, priced again as one order, and its issued quotations by number, up to 10, each found in its history under the party and the sales area and read as it was issued, whole or the items it names: at least one line or document, counted at most 600 crates, each line's part crate counted whole, typically some 20 trucks; more is `ANSWER_TOO_LARGE`, to plan fewer at once. Each is asked before the planner runs whether it is loaded, and any that is not refuses the whole plan, `422 NOT_PLANNABLE`, its message naming each with its mend, the first 10 and how many more: an inquiry is never planned, neither an issued inquiry by its number nor an inquiry profile's line, its material's sales status blocking it for delivery (TVMS's `SPVBJ`), as an inquiry profile has no die yet and no packing values; nor a quotation never issued to the customer in the sales area, another's answered alike, a revoked one, an item the quotation does not hold, a line pricing does not answer `ok`, or packing data LINKIN lacks, such as a coated pack with no measured face, which the customer asks its sales representative at LINKIN to have fixed. The planner packs each line's packs into crates as long as its bars, at least their carrier's shortest, a line's full crates its own and the rests of lines of one cut length sharing crates, by profile, then colour, then quotation; stands them side by side across the planning vehicle, a standard curtainsider semi-trailer, and stacks them under a margin to its roof, about four full crates high, a shorter crate on a longer one flush with its front end, under its legal payload: each line and item answers how the order names it, each carrier its inside and what it weighs empty, and each truck its crates where they stand — what each holds, line by line, and a coated crate's packs in bands — its goods' net and gross weight, how much of it they take and what they leave `free`. Up to 5 articles `fill` names, each a line or an issued item the plan loads, are each planned again with more full packs, to find a number of them with which a plan still takes as many trucks (`fills`): a plan made, never the most nor that any smaller amount fits; a search its count of plans or the deadline stops first is answered unfinished. The weights are theoretical, each crate's own empty weight LINKIN's estimate, and the axles not checked. SAP plans a load in TM alone, on a sales order's freight unit, which a quotation never reaches: the plan is the API's own.

Lists a customer's quotations in one sales area, newest first, in batches, to find one again. The MCP server reads them. A customer lists only its own.

post.summary: Issue the order as a quotation
post.description:
Turns a priced order into a quotation: a numbered offer with two pages, which its customer can read, submit, or revoke while it is a draft. A quotation is for own and catalogue profiles, which LINKIN can make today; a new profile needs an inquiry. The MCP server tells the assistant to call it only once the customer has seen the price and said yes. It issues only at the prices shown: if a price moved since, nothing is issued, and the customer is asked again. The same order issued twice in a day answers the same quotation, so a retry never makes two.

Issues the order `evaluate_order` answered as a quotation, VA21's: the offer, which its customer submits to LINKIN (`submit_quotation`) for LINKIN to release. Issued = shown: the body is the order `evaluate_order` answered, issued as a document its `issuableAs` names — `quotation` by `issue_quotation`, `inquiry` by `issue_inquiry` — with `expected`, the `inputHash` and `priceHash` it answered, and none of what its answer carried (`only`, `view`, `detailItems`). The `201` answers its number, id, status and URL. It stands `draft`, numbered and kept, not binding until LINKIN releases it. An order issues as a quotation only where every line is `ok`, none refused or to be locked (`VCH_HL_CORE/038`, SAP saves no such configuration as released), and no item's material's sales status blocks quotations — an inquiry profile, whose die does not exist yet (TVMS through `MVKE-VMSTA`); else `NOT_ISSUABLE`, its message naming the first line keeping it out, why, how many more lines do, and what the order is issuable as. get.summary: An issued quotation, its summary page
get.description:
The quotation's summary page, for a person: its items, prices and terms, as issued. Its customer opens it from the link issuing answers. Another customer's quotation answers as if it did not exist. It never changes, except one line that shows its current status.

The summary a customer reads: the order's facts, each position with its figures and its processes, the totals and the terms, each position linked to its bill on the details page, `GET /customer/v1/quotations/{id}/details`. Under its letterhead a status line says where the document stands now, in fixed words dated by the day it came to stand so: a draft quotation "a preview, not binding until LINKIN releases it", an open inquiry "Open since" its day, its title and lead saying it is preliminary, a submitted quotation "Submitted on" its day, "not binding until LINKIN releases it", a released quotation "Released on" its day, and any other status "Not binding". The page as it was issued, for a browser: its stylesheets inlined, no script, laid out for a phone as for a desktop and printable as paper, the two pages linking each other relatively. It never changes but for its status line, yet is kept for the browser alone and revalidated by its ETag on each opening, so a page withdrawn leaves every cache; it loads nothing but its own styles, fonts and icon (`Content-Security-Policy`), sends no referrer, is not indexed, and carries no CORS header.

The quotation's summary.

parameters.description: The id `POST /customer/v1/quotations` issued it under: 32 hex digits, never the document's number.

post.summary: Issue the order as an inquiry
post.description:
Turns a priced order of new profiles into an inquiry: a numbered, preliminary offer with two pages. Each new profile needs a new die, so its price holds only after LINKIN's technical review. The MCP server tells the assistant to call it only once the customer has seen the price and said yes. It issues only at the prices shown, and the same order issued twice in a day answers the same inquiry. A new customer, with no customer number in SAP yet, may only issue inquiries, at most 20 a day. Its customer may revoke it while it stands open.

Issues the order `evaluate_order` answered as an inquiry, VA11's: the preliminary offer, not binding until a technical review of the product — the quotation's page in its own words, marked non-binding. Issued = shown: the body is the order `evaluate_order` answered, issued as a document its `issuableAs` names — `quotation` by `issue_quotation`, `inquiry` by `issue_inquiry` — with `expected`, the `inputHash` and `priceHash` it answered, and none of what its answer carried (`only`, `view`, `detailItems`). The order is evaluated again and issued only where both hashes hold: two self-contained HTML pages — the summary, the head, every item with its configuration, quantity, price per unit, net value and processes, and the total; the details, each item's price breakdown line by line as V/08 prints it — frozen as issued, stored under a new id that cannot be guessed, served at `GET /customer/v1/inquiries/{id}` and `GET /customer/v1/inquiries/{id}/details`, its JSON at `GET /customer/v1/inquiries/{id}/document`, and numbered LINKIN's own way. The `201` answers its number, id, status and URL. It stands `open`, non-binding and open to review. The status words: `draft`, a quotation as issued, not binding until LINKIN releases it; `submitted`, a quotation its customer submitted to LINKIN (`submit_quotation`), final, not binding until LINKIN releases it; `released`, a quotation LINKIN released, binding; `open`, non-binding — an inquiry, open to review; `revoked`, withdrawn by its customer, or by LINKIN before 2.0.0, not to be acted on. Any other word, one a later version adds, is read as `revoked`: not to be acted on.

Idempotent by its content for a day: the same order — the same party, lines and references, however written — at the prices shown, issued again, answers the first document's `201`, never a second document, so a retry after a timeout is safe; it answers where that document stands now. A document since revoked or erased no longer holds its order: the same order is issued anew.

An order issues as an inquiry only where every line is `ok`, none refused or to be locked (`VCH_HL_CORE/038`, SAP saves no such configuration as released), and no item's material's sales status blocks inquiries — a profile the plant can make, which is quoted (TVMS through `MVKE-VMSTA`); else `NOT_ISSUABLE`, its message naming the first line keeping it out, why, how many more lines do, and what the order is issuable as. get.description:
The inquiry's details page, for a person: each item's specification and its bill, charge by charge. It shows why an item costs what it does. Another customer's inquiry answers as if it did not exist. It never changes, except one line that shows its current status.

Each position's specification and its bill line by line — each charge with its basis and the rules that billed it — linked back to its row on the summary, `GET /customer/v1/inquiries/{id}`. Under its letterhead a status line says where the document stands now, in fixed words dated by the day it came to stand so: a draft quotation "a preview, not binding until LINKIN releases it", an open inquiry "Open since" its day, its title and lead saying it is preliminary, a submitted quotation "Submitted on" its day, "not binding until LINKIN releases it", a released quotation "Released on" its day, and any other status "Not binding". The page as it was issued, for a browser: its stylesheets inlined, no script, laid out for a phone as for a desktop and printable as paper, the two pages linking each other relatively. It never changes but for its status line, yet is kept for the browser alone and revalidated by its ETag on each opening, so a page withdrawn leaves every cache; it loads nothing but its own styles, fonts and icon (`Content-Security-Policy`), sends no referrer, is not indexed, and carries no CORS header.

The inquiry's details.

get.description:
The inquiry's content as data, exactly as issued, for a program to show in its own layout. The MCP server reads it to show a document again. A long one comes in parts. Another customer's inquiry answers as if it did not exist.

The inquiry as it was issued, a page at a time: where it stands now — its status and since when — then its head on the first page — the versions, the header with its Incoterms, the totals, the minimum groups — and its rows, each an item's facts, specification in a line, entered values, quantity, net price and value and its processes. A page holds at most `limit` rows and no more than fit 40000 bytes of its JSON as sent, compact — about 47 rows — with `total` and, while more remain, `next`: pass it as `after` for the next page. One item's charges and specification in rows are `get_inquiry_items`'s. Its content never changes, keeping the shape of the `contractVersion` its head carries; where it stands lives, read off its envelope at each call. Revoked, it answers its envelope alone, `revoked`, the day and, where its customer revoked it, `revocation`. It carries the page's guards and no CORS header. Erased, or issued before its content was kept, an inquiry has none: `404`. The same document as a page for a person is `GET /customer/v1/inquiries/{id}`.

A page of the inquiry's document; revoked, its envelope alone.

First, `INVALID_REQUEST` with no `pointer` for a call without the sign-in, with one LINKIN did not write, or with its person's details refused; then the same for the details of the customer the call acts for, or whose document it reads, refused. `ANSWER_TOO_LARGE` (`pointer` `/limit`): the page would pass the largest answer: ask for fewer at a time with `limit`.

get.description:
Each item's specification and its bill, charge by charge, as data: the details page for a program. The MCP server reads it when a customer asks why an item costs what it does. Items can be asked for by number. Another customer's inquiry answers as if it did not exist.

The inquiry's items in detail, each as `evaluate_order`'s detail answers a line and as it was issued: its specification in rows, its bill by process with every charge — its quantity, rate, basis and the rules that billed it, a statistical one not added again — and its shares of the minimum groups. Every item, or those `items` names, `items=30,10`: 1 to 50 item numbers, answered in the document's order; a number the document has not is refused, the message listing every such number. Either list is paged alike: at most `limit` items and no more than fit 40000 bytes of the page's JSON as sent, compact — about 9 items — with `total`, the document's, and while more remain `next`, to pass as `after` with the same `items`. Why one item costs what it does is `items` with its number; its row is `get_inquiry`'s. Revoked, the items are gone: `410`.

post.description:
Withdraws an open inquiry no longer wanted, with the reason why: the inquiry stays in its history, revoked, beside its reason. It is its customer's act, with its own sign-in or through the MCP server when the customer asks to revoke that inquiry; anyone signed in for the same customer may revoke it, and a new customer's inquiry only the sign-in that issued it.

Revokes an issued open inquiry, by its customer: it stands `revoked` from the sales organization's day, its JSON answering its envelope with `revocation`, its two pages `410`, and the same inquiry issued again is a new one. The body names the sold-to party and the sales area the inquiry was issued to — LINKIN's 1102 / 10, the inquiry's, whichever area the sign-in lists the customer in; LINKIN's one-time customer for a sign-in linked to none — another party's or area's the `404` of an unknown inquiry, and why: `reason`, one of LINKIN's reasons for rejection by its code, and `note`, in its giver's own words, required with `ZZ`. One revoked already answers as it stands, its first day and reason kept. The `200` answers what issuing answered, its status `revoked`, with `revokedOn` and `revocation`.

The inquiry revoked, or as it stands where it was revoked before: its number, id, status and page's URL, what it was issued for, the day it was revoked and why.

ApiError.description: Any error status: what went wrong with the request, never with a value — a value problem is inside a 200 document with a status.

code.description: What the request was refused for. `INTERNAL` is the one the caller cannot mend and says no more: the cause is logged, never sent. The `message`, `retryable` and `safeToRetry` say the rest of a code a reader does not know. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `INTERNAL`.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed later: true where a store was not reached or an order ran past its deadline (`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`), false for every refusal of the request and for what fails the same way again — the model's own failure among it.

safeToRetry.description: Whether repeating the request is harmless: always, issuing, submitting and revoking included. An issue is kept a day under its content: a repeat within the day answers the document first issued; after that document is revoked or erased, or the day is out, the same order issues a new one. A submission or a revocation repeated answers where the document stands, its first day and reason kept.

requestId.description: The request's id, which LINKIN traces it by, so a report finds it.

pointer.description: Where in the request's body the refusal is, an RFC 6901 pointer — `/items/2/quantity`, `/values/ZA_TEMPER` — where it is one part of the body; a member the body lacks where its absence is refused (`/soldToParty`). A query parameter refused is named the same way by its name in this document, as a tool generated from it takes it: `/after`.

Assortment.description: `GET /customer/v1/assortment`: a page of what the customer orders, and how the press makes bars of it.

profiles.description: The page's profiles: the party's own geometries first, in the release list's order, then the catalogue profiles of the sales area, in the model's.

next.description: The cursor of the next page, its request's `after`; absent on the last. The order profiles is listed in never changes from page to page.

total.description: How many profiles the request lists, on every page. A whole number.

AssortmentProfile.description: One profile the customer orders — the party's own geometry, released to it in the plant's release list, or a catalogue profile of the sales area — with the facts an order of it is decided by, read off the master data and the configuration the geometry gives. The die's number is a minimum group's key alone.

kind.description: `own` a geometry released to the party, `catalogue` a profile any customer of the sales area orders, its geometry the material's own. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `catalogue`.

geometryText.description: The geometry's text, where the model holds one.

material.description: The material it is ordered as.

orderAs.description: An order line's template: the material and the values to enter for the profile — the geometry of an own one, none for a catalogue one, whose geometry is its classification's. The quantity, the finish and the rest are the order's.

items.description: One pack of the packaging list for a finish, what the order quantity's user exit packs by. Each line's quantity is lifted to the smallest `minimum` of its finish's packs, then rounded up: whole steps of the largest `rounding`, the rest one step of the smallest `rounding` at least as large. `pieces` only counts packs.

finish.description: The surface finish, its Values-tab key.

minimum.description: This pack's minimum on the list; only the smallest of its finish's binds: a line's quantity is lifted to it, a catalogue article made to length to at least 600. A pack is used below its own. In pieces, `H87`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

rounding.description: The pieces one step of this pack adds. In pieces, `H87`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

pieces.description: The pieces a full pack holds: the line's pieces in this bundle over it, rounded up, are its packs of it, the last possibly part-full. It never moves the quantity. In pieces, `H87`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

packs.description: The packaging list's packs, per finish; a finish the list has no row for is not offered on the geometry.

length.description: The lengths a piece is cut to: the cut length's domain once the geometry is given. An anodized or flash-anodized piece over 7,000 mm is not made, which the domain's one interval does not show: an order there is inconsistent.

min.description: The shortest. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

max.description: The longest. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

unit.description: The lengths' unit. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

barMax.description: The longest bar the press runs for the profile: the saw's, or the die's where that is shorter. Anodized or flash-anodized, the bar is at most 7,000 mm, and a longer piece is refused.

items.description: A bar of the geometry the stock list keeps.

stage.description: The process stage, its Values-tab key.

length.description: The bar's length. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

unit.description: The length's unit. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

stockLengths.description: The stock list's bars of the geometry: a list, not availability.

items.description: A minimum per order the profile's lines are grouped under, as the order's groups name it: the press run's and the die wear's minimum per die.

minimumGroups.description: The minimums per order the profile shares with every line on the same key.

weightPerMetre.description: The profile's theoretical weight per metre, a thermal break's its halves' and its strips': a line's weights are computed from it, not weighed.

perimeter.description: The profile's perimeter, what a finish covers.

BandPacks.description: One line's or issued quotation's item's packs in a band of a crate: its count of packs there alone, its pieces and net weight standing in the crate's `contents`.

document.description: The issued quotation the item is of, by its number; absent for a line of the body.

item.description: The line's item, or the issued quotation's (`VBAP-POSNR`).

BarRules.description: How the press makes bars, as the model reckons them: under the plant's cutting optimization whole pieces fill the longest bar the saw allows, a kerf between two, an offcut where the pieces are shorter than it; without it a bar a piece; either way the bar lifted to the press's shortest and, coated, to the powder line's, a piece shorter than its bar cut from it. Data for a cutting optimizer; the order's own bars stay authoritative.

kerf.description: The saw's kerf between two pieces of a bar. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

offcut.description: The shortest remnant the machining centre processes: a bar of shorter pieces keeps its last `offcut` as an offcut, a bar of longer ones none. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

minimum.description: The shortest bar the press delivers. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

coatedMinimum.description: The shortest bar the powder line takes, coated. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

maximum.description: The longest bar the saw delivers; a profile's `barMax` may be shorter, and an anodized or flash-anodized bar is at most 7,000 mm. Whole millimetres today: the model's lengths hold no decimals (CT04). In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

unit.description: The lengths' unit. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

BoundTerm.description: A term of the plan's bound: `weight`, the crates' gross weight against the payload; `space`, their length times height against the lanes the truck holds across, its length and its stack height (`TruckFill.space`); `longCrates`, the crates longer than a part of the truck, which stand at most so many behind one another and so many high. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `space`.

Charge.description: One printed condition line of an item's bill (`KOMV`), keyed by its V/08 step (`STUNR`), since one condition type may price an item more than once: its text and value, the quantity and rate it is made of where the quotation's columns say so, a percentage's rate, its basis as the quotation's sentence says it, and the rules that billed it. A `statistical` line (`KOMV-KSTAT`) builds the price and is not added again: never sum it with the others.

text.description: The condition type's text, as the bill prints it.

value.description: The line's value, `KWERT`. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

percentage.description: A percentage condition's rate (calculation type `A`), in percent: `3.5` is 3.5 %. At the precision the engine computed it, in its shortest digits.

basis.description: The basis in one sentence, as the quotation's breakdown prints it.

minimum.description: Whether it bills a minimum: a minimum billable quantity per item, or a share of a minimum per order.

perOrder.description: Whether it is the item's share of an amount for the whole order: a group condition's.

statistical.description: `KOMV-KSTAT`: it builds the price and is not added again.

ChargeQuantity.description: The quantity a charge's rate applied to, as the quotation's column reads it: the condition's basis (`KAWRT`) in its unit, or the characteristic the procedure took the factor from, in that characteristic's unit — a count by the piece in `H87` or none.

value.description: In `unit`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, three in any other; with no unit, as the engine computed it.

unit.description: Its unit. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

ChargeRate.description: A charge's rate: the record's amount (`KBETR`) in its currency, `per` so many of `unit` (`KPEIN`, `KMEIN`) — no unit on a fixed amount.

amount.description: The rate, in `currency`, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

per.description: How many of `unit` the amount is for. At the precision the engine computed it, in its shortest digits.

unit.description: The unit it is per. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

ConfigurationDocument.description: `POST /customer/v1/materials/{material}/configuration`: the screen. Every characteristic of the class with one status, its value, what decided it and its options; the order item as the user exits left it, with its pricing; the issues; the selections a level below would now make differently.

fields.description: Every characteristic of the class the screen shows, in screen order.

issues.description: What is wrong or missing, each on the level it is about. On a customer's screen, while a field reads `required` or its entry is refused for its value (`INVALID_CHARACTERISTIC_VALUE`), a `REQUIRED_CHARACTERISTIC` on such a field's name — on the root, or on a level below — and `MISSING_SELECTION_VALUE`, the class item's selection waiting on their values, are left out: the fields, the refusal and the status say them. Every other message stays.

lock.description: Selections a level below would now make differently: SAP's "the configuration must be locked by the user before saving".

ConfigurationRequest.description: `POST /customer/v1/materials/{material}/configuration`: the body — the whole entry, every time.

values.description: The entered values by CT04 name, as the user typed or picked them; a name the class does not allocate, or on `/customer/v1` one an order cannot enter, is `UNKNOWN_CHARACTERISTIC`. A value is a string, or a number, read as its text.

quantity.description: The order quantity, in the material's unit: required, as on every order line. A JSON number, positive, of at most its unit's decimals — none in `H87`, the piece: a string is refused, `INVALID_REQUEST`, and more decimals or a quantity not above zero `INVALID_QUANTITY`, each with its `pointer`.

unit.description: The unit `quantity` is in: the Rec 20 code of the material's own unit, `MaterialSummary.unit` — `H87` for the piece — the one unit an entry takes; the material's where omitted. Any other code, SAP's `PC` and `ST` among them, is refused, `INVALID_REQUEST`, with its `pointer`.

soldToParty.description: The order header's sold-to party, `VBAK-KUNNR`, required on `/customer/v1` where the material's `readsSoldToParty` is true: a customer number of at most 10 characters, digits alone read with their leading zeros (`9999999` is `0009999999`), one the customer master holds and extends to the sales area, else `UNKNOWN_SOLD_TO_PARTY`. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

salesOrganization.description: `VBAK-VKORG`, required with the distribution channel: the item is priced there. An area no material is sold in is `UNKNOWN_SALES_AREA`; a material not sold there is `MATERIAL_NOT_IN_SALES_AREA` where it is sold in another sales area the sign-in acts in, and the path's `404 UNKNOWN_MATERIAL` where in none, the inquiry's material aside.

ConfigurationStatus.description: `ok` complete and consistent; `incomplete` consistent with values still to enter; `inconsistent` an entry a dependency or the characteristic's format refuses, as an order's line says it. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `inconsistent`.

CrateBand.description: A band of rows of packs across a crate, all of one profile's face and one way round, whichever stands lower for the band's packs, the face as measured where both stand as high, and the carrier's full count the way it holds the most, the face as measured where both hold as many: the face of a full pack as measured, whether its packs lie turned, how many a full row holds, how many rows the band stands, and each line's packs in it. The packs fill the band in the order of its entries, from its bottom (the crate's floor, or the top of the band under it), left to right from the crate's left side, the truck's left, row by row: a row may hold the end of one entry and the start of the next, and only the band's top row may be part, its packs from the left. A part pack counts whole. Each row stands as high as the face's `height`, or its `width` where turned, so the band `rows` times that, and the crate's bands as high as the sum of theirs, with no gap. Packs of one profile lying one way round share a band, so two bands one on the other never hold them; two bands of different profiles may measure alike. That is a convention for a drawing, not how the plant packs a crate.

width.description: A full pack's width, as measured. In millimetres, to hundredths.

height.description: A full pack's height, as measured. In millimetres, to hundredths.

turned.description: Whether each pack lies turned, its height across the crate and its width up; else its width across.

across.description: The packs a full row of the face holds across the crate.

rows.description: The rows the band stands: its packs over `across`, rounded up.

packs.description: Each line's packs in the band, in the order they fill it: at most `rows` times `across` in all.

CrateContent.description: What a crate holds of one line or one issued quotation's item, which `document` and `item` name together.

document.description: The issued quotation the item is of, by its number; absent for a line of the body.

item.description: The line's item, or the issued quotation's (`VBAP-POSNR`).

packs.description: Its packs in the crate, where they travel inside it by their face; absent where the crate is the pack.

netWeight.description: Its pieces' net weight, theoretical, the crate's own left out. In kilograms, `KGM`, to its decimals: none in `H87`, the piece, three in any other unit.

DocumentKind.description: A sales document an order is issued as: the `quotation`, VA21's, the offer, issued `draft` and not binding until LINKIN releases it, `POST /customer/v1/quotations`; or the `inquiry`, VA11's, the preliminary offer, `POST /customer/v1/inquiries`. A sales order never enters it, nor `issuableAs`: the API issues pre-sales documents alone. A kind a later version adds reads as `inquiry`, and a reader offers to issue no kind it does not know. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `inquiry`.

DocumentStatus.description: Where an issued document stands, each word meaning one thing: `draft`, a quotation as issued — numbered, a preview not binding until LINKIN releases it, and its customer may revoke it; `submitted`, a quotation its customer submitted to LINKIN (1.1.0), final — the customer can neither change nor withdraw it — and not binding until LINKIN releases it; `released`, a quotation LINKIN released, binding as SAP's released quotation is; `open`, an inquiry, SAP's preliminary offer, non-binding and open to review, which its customer may revoke; `revoked`, since its `statusOn`, withdrawn — a draft quotation or an open inquiry by its customer, with its reason (2.0.0), or by LINKIN before 2.0.0 — a document not to be acted on. A status a later version adds reads as `revoked`: not to be acted on. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `revoked`.

ExpectedHashes.description: What issuing holds the order to: the `inputHash` and `priceHash` `POST /customer/v1/order` answered the order the caller showed. An order whose own `inputHash` is not `expected.inputHash` is `ORDER_DIFFERS`; evaluated again, one whose prices moved is `PRICES_CHANGED`. The order's `inputHash` and `expected.priceHash` are what the issue is kept under for a day.

FieldControl.description: The control a field takes: a list where CT04 has a Values tab, a number for a NUM characteristic, text otherwise. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `text`.

FieldDefinition.description: `GET /customer/v1/materials/{material}`: one characteristic of the material's class, as CT04 and the class define it before anything is entered. Static: a UI fetches it once per model version.

text.description: `CHARC_TXT`: the characteristic's description, or its name where it has none.

dataType.description: The CT04 format. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `CHAR`.

values.description: The Values tab, as the class allows it, each value with its text.

interval.description: The interval a NUM characteristic admits.

from.description: The lowest value, in the characteristic's unit and to its decimals.

to.description: The highest value, in the characteristic's unit and to its decimals.

unit.description: CT04's unit of the characteristic. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

notReadyForInput.description: Valued by a dependency, never entered.

FieldGroup.description: The characteristic group a field belongs to: one section of the screen. Fields come in screen order — the profile's groups in their sorting order, each group's fields in its sequence, then the fields no group names — so consecutive fields with one group are one section.

FieldInputControl.description: The UI input control the material's characteristic group gives a field (Manage Characteristic Groups, *UI Control*). Absent where the group sets none, or the field is in no group. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `default`.

FieldOption.description: One option of a list: a Values-tab value, disabled where the other entries rule it out; the value held where the list lacks it, an entry refused, disabled too.

disabled.description: Ruled out by what the other entries decided, or the value held that the list lacks.

FieldState.description: One field of the form, as the evaluated configuration leaves it.

text.description: `CHARC_TXT`: the characteristic's description, or its name where it has none.

heading.description: `CABNT-ATUE1`: the first line of the characteristic's heading, its short name, where it has one. A document's specification, and a line's `specification`, name the field by it; `text` names it where it stands alone, as on the screen.

dataType.description: The CT04 format. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `CHAR`.

required.description: Whether the field must be valued: entry required in the class, or a selection condition decidedly true for the values entered so far.

value.description: The value as data: every digit the configuration holds, never a tilde — but a refused entry, echoed as it was sent. An enterable field's value goes back in `values` as it is.

valueText.description: `VALUE_TXT`: the value's description where the Values tab has one, otherwise the value as AVC's screen shows it — an inferred or default number with more decimals than CT04 shows rounded to them behind a tilde (`~4.874` for 4.8735); an entry the Values tab, as the class allows it, refuses reads as entered.

by.description: What decided the status where a dependency did — the constraint, the table, the class — named with its level where that is below the root.

options.description: The list a list control offers: the values the constraints leave, the ruled-out ones disabled with what ruled them out, and a held value the list lacks kept, disabled, so a rejected entry stays visible. On a screen only; an order's lines carry no options. A customer's screen carries them on a field open to input — `entered`, `conflict`, `default`, `required`, `optional` — an entered one's as the other entries leave it, and only where the list holds at most 50: a longer one is searched through `POST /customer/v1/value-help`.

optionCount.description: How many options the list holds, carried inline or not: on every list field of a screen, absent on an order's line. A whole number.

interval.description: The interval a NUM characteristic admits.

from.description: The lowest value, in the characteristic's unit and to its decimals.

to.description: The highest value, in the characteristic's unit and to its decimals.

unit.description: CT04's unit of the characteristic. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

FieldStatus.description: Where a field of the form stands. `entered` and `conflict` are the user's own values, the second one a dependency rejects; `default` a `?=` default valued it and an entry overwrites it; `inferred` a dependency decided it, `external` master data fixed it; `hidden` a precondition keeps it off the screen; `not-ready` a dependency has yet to value it; `required` and `optional` are open for input. Open: a value a later version adds reads as `not-ready`.

FieldValue.description: A value of a Values tab as a UI shows it: the key an entry sends, and the text the screen shows for it — the value's CT04 description, or the value itself where it has none.

FillSentence.description: The sentence of an article `fill` names, with its line or item, as `contents` names one: a quotation's `document` and `item`, or a line's `item` alone.

document.description: The quotation's number, where the article is one of its items.

item.description: `VBAP-POSNR`, the line or item, as `lines` and `documents` number it.

sentence.description: What a plan with more packs of it took, in plain words.

GroupBasis.description: The basis a minimum is spread by: the group's lines' bases summed — kilograms through a die, metres of its wear, square metres of a colour — to its unit's decimals; or, with no unit, their value in the document's currency — the order's anodizing — to the currency's decimals.

value.description: The basis, to its unit's decimals; with no unit, an amount in the document's currency, to the currency's.

unit.description: The basis's unit. Its UN/ECE Recommendation 20 common code — the table in the document's description — with SAP's internal key beside it.

sapUnit.description: SAP's internal key of `unit` (`T006-MSEHI`), which no logon language changes: `ST` for the piece, which SD's English screens print `PC`.

GroupMember.description: One line of a group: its item, its basis — its part of the group's, in the group's unit and to its decimals, or in the document's currency where the group's basis has no unit — and its share of the uplift, SAP's `AMIZ` on the item: what the minimum lifts the line by.

basis.description: Its basis, in the group's unit, to its decimals; with no unit on the group's, an amount in the document's currency.

share.description: Its share of the uplift. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

GroupShare.description: A line's part of a minimum group it shares: the group's `id`, the line's basis in the group's unit, and its share of the uplift, SAP's `AMIZ` on the item.

basis.description: Its basis, in the group's unit, to its decimals; with no unit on the group's, an amount in the document's currency.

share.description: Its share of the uplift. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

GroupSummary.description: A minimum group as an issued document's head keeps it: an `OrderGroup` without its members, each item carrying its own part as `shares`.

id.description: Opaque, unique in the document: its rows and items name the group by it.

key.description: What its lines share: the die, the colour, the anodizing's one key.

value.description: What the lines bill themselves. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

minimum.description: The minimum. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

uplift.description: What the lines are lifted by: the minimum less the value. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

HealthDocument.description: `GET /public/v1/health`: the service is up, and on which model.

modelVersion.description: The model version: the version of LINKIN's products, rules and prices the API holds, as every quotation prints it.

materials.description: How many materials a sales order can configure.

HelpValue.description: One value of the characteristic's list.

text.description: The text the screen shows for it: its CT04 description, or the value where it has none.

allowed.description: Whether the other entries leave it. On a material that reads the sold-to party a customer's list holds the allowed values alone: the others may be another customer's.

reason.description: Why a value not allowed is out: `VCH_HL_DEP_TRACE/005`, the constraint that restricted the characteristic's domain, on the level it is bound on.

HistoryEntry.description: One document of the customer's history: what the index by customer (SAP's `VAKPA`) holds of it, and its page's URL.

number.description: LINKIN's number, ten characters: `LQ26000000` a quotation's, `LI26000000` an inquiry's.

url.description: Where its summary page opens, as issuing answered it: a customer's document's, the page's absolute URL on LINKIN's API.

issuedOn.description: The pricing date it was priced on, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

netValue.description: The order's net value in `currency`, excluding VAT; absent where nothing was priced. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.

soldToPartyName.description: The sold-to party's name as the document was issued to it, SAP's *Name 1*: a customer's `KNA1-NAME1`; a one-time customer's, the document's own address's. Absent on a document issued before the name was kept with it.

submittedOn.description: The day it was submitted, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the sales organization's zone, where it was.

revokedOn.description: The day it was revoked, `YYYY-MM-DD`, where it was: by its customer, in the sales organization's zone; by LINKIN, before 2.0.0, in UTC.

revocation.description: Why it was revoked, where it was: its customer's reason.

Incoterms.description: The Incoterms the order is delivered under, `VBKD-INCO1` and `-INCO2_L`: the sold-to party's, as its sales area data (`KNVV-INCO1`, `-INCO2_L`) gives them — today `EXW`, ex works, at the plant in Plovdiv, for every customer. Absent on an order without a sold-to party, or one with no sales area data where the order is placed.

InquiryHistory.description: `GET /customer/v1/inquiries`: a page of the customer's inquiries, newest first.

next.description: The cursor of the next page, for `after`; absent on the last.

InquiryItemRequest.description: `POST /customer/v1/inquiries`: one item of the inquiry, an inquiry profile under the customer's name for it — its configuration off the drawing and the pieces it is offered for, each required.

item.description: `VBAP-POSNR`, the item's number: 1 to 6 digits, its leading zeros dropped (`000010` is `10`), each once, never zero. Every item numbers itself or none does — a mix is `INVALID_REQUEST` — and where none does they are 10, 20, 30 by their place. Lines, messages and groups name the item by it.

customerItem.description: `VBAP-POSEX`, the customer's purchase order item: at most 6 characters, echoed on the line. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

customerMaterial.description: `VBAP-KDMAT`: the customer's name for the profile, at most 35 characters, which titles its row. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

material.description: An inquiry profile, a material whose sales status keeps it out of quotations.

values.description: The profile's values by CT04 name, off the drawing. A value is a string, or a number, read as its text.

quantity.description: The pieces the preliminary offer is priced for, in the material's unit. A JSON number, positive, of at most its unit's decimals — none in `H87`, the piece: a string is refused, `INVALID_REQUEST`, and more decimals or a quantity not above zero `INVALID_QUANTITY`, each with its `pointer`.

unit.description: The unit `quantity` is in: the Rec 20 code of the material's own unit, `MaterialSummary.unit` — `H87` for the piece — the one unit an entry takes; the material's where omitted. Any other code, SAP's `PC` and `ST` among them, is refused, `INVALID_REQUEST`, with its `pointer`.

customerReference.description: `VBKD-BSTKD` on the item, as an order's: at most 35 characters. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

InquiryRequest.description: `POST /customer/v1/inquiries`: the body — the customer the preliminary offer is for, its references, the items and the hashes the order was shown with. `POST /customer/v1/quotations`' body with the customer and their RFQ reference, and each item's name for the profile, quantity and values, required. Where the customer is the one-time customer, the inquiry is addressed to the buyer by the sign-in, their registration on the LINKIN website: the body takes no address (since 2.0.0).

salesOrganization.description: `VBAK-VKORG`, required with the distribution channel: an item whose material is not sold there is refused on its line, `V1/382` where it is sold in another sales area the sign-in acts in, `UNKNOWN_MATERIAL` where in none, the inquiry's material aside.

soldToParty.description: `VBAK-KUNNR`, the order header's sold-to party, one for every item: a customer number of at most 10 characters, digits alone read with their leading zeros (`9999999` is `0009999999`), one the customer master holds and extends to the sales area, else `UNKNOWN_SOLD_TO_PARTY`. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

customerReference.description: `VBKD-BSTKD`, the customer's reference for the document, its Cust. reference: at most 35 characters, printed on the issued document as given. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

reference.description: `VBAK-XBLNR`, the document's own reference: at most 16 characters, printed on the issued document as its reference. It holds no control, bidirectional or invisible character, Unicode 17.0.0's default-ignorable code points among them but ZWNJ, ZWJ and the variation selectors: those the pattern names, and U+1BCA0 to U+1BCA3, U+1D173 to U+1D17A, U+E0000 to U+E00FF and U+E01F0 to U+E0FFF, beyond U+FFFF. Its length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as SAP counts a CHAR field: a character beyond U+FFFF counts two.

items.description: At least one, at most 300: more is `TOO_MANY_ITEMS`.

IssuedDocument.description: `GET /customer/v1/quotations/{id}/document` and the inquiry's: a page of the document as it was issued. First where it stands now, its envelope — kind, number, status and the day it came to stand so, the sold-to party, the pricing day and the instant of issue — then, frozen at issue, its head on the first page alone and its rows, at most `limit` and as many as fit 40000 bytes of the page's JSON as sent, compact, with how many rows it has and the cursor of the next page. A revoked document answers its envelope alone, why it was revoked with it.

statusOn.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`: the day it came to stand as `status` says — its pricing day at issue; a submission's and a revocation's, in the sales organization's zone; LINKIN's revocation's, before 2.0.0, in UTC.

customerVerified.description: Whether LINKIN stands behind the customer's details: `true` for a customer LINKIN linked the sign-in to; `false` where they are a website registration's, the one-time customer's company and contact details from the sign-in's registration on the LINKIN website and not yet verified by LINKIN — not to be taken as the sender's identity until it is validated (since 1.2.0). Always written; absent, read as `false`.

issuedAt.description: The instant it was issued, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second.

revocation.description: Why it was revoked, where it was: its customer's reason.

rows.description: The rows of the page, in the order's order.

total.description: How many rows the document has; absent on a revoked one.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; absent on the last.

IssuedHead.description: What an issued document holds as a whole, frozen at issue: the versions it was issued under — it answers in their shape, a field a later version adds on the documents issued under that version alone — the header, the totals, the minimum groups without their members, and the order's own messages.

contractVersion.description: The contract's semver it was issued under.

modelVersion.description: The model's version it was priced under.

groups.description: The minimum groups, without their members.

messages.description: What the order said as a whole.

IssuedItems.description: `GET /customer/v1/quotations/{id}/document/items` and the inquiry's: an issued document's items in detail, each as `evaluate_order`'s detail answers a line — a page of every item, or of those `items` names, at most `limit` and as many as fit 40000 bytes of the page's JSON as sent — with how many items the document has and the cursor of the next page.

items.description: The items, in the document's order.

total.description: How many items the document has.

next.description: The cursor of the next page, of every item or of those `items` names; absent on the last.

IssuedRow.description: One row of an issued document, frozen at issue: an item's facts, its description and its specification in a line, the values it entered, its quantity as entered and ordered, its net price and value, its uplift and groups, and its processes without their charges — `…/document/items` answers the item with them.

customerReference.description: `VBKD-BSTKD` on the item, as the order gave it.

text.description: The specification in one short line, the product's own values, then the first value of each further step, each value once, the geometry with its description: `7099999 · Window frame · T5, standard · 4500 mm · Powder coated`. The rows the quotation prints are the item's `specification`.

values.description: The values the order entered, by CT04 name: what a repeat of the line sends as its `values`.

netValue.description: `VBAP-NETWR`, the binding figure; absent on a line not priced. In the document currency, to its decimals: two in `EUR`.
